original_question: For sets of reals, are the selection principles U_fin(Γ, Ω) and S_fin(Γ, Ω) equivalent, where Γ is the family of open γ-covers and Ω is the family of open ω-covers? If they are not equivalent, does the Hurewicz-type property U_fin(Γ, Γ) nevertheless imply S_fin(Γ, Ω)?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 1 ([24, Problems 1 and 2]), on the two remaining unsettled implications in the classical open-cover diagram for sets of reals. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the right ambient setting (sets of reals), the right cover classes Γ and Ω, the right comparison U_fin(Γ,Ω) vs. S_fin(Γ,Ω), and the right fallback question asking whether the Hurewicz property U_fin(Γ,Γ) implies S_fin(Γ,Ω). This is essentially Section 4, Problem 1, with “Hurewicz-type property” correctly identifying U_fin(Γ,Γ). ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s variable is a set of reals X (more generally, spaces homeomorphic to sets of reals unless otherwise indicated), so the question should be stated as a property of a specific X. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
A “cover” in the paper is nontrivial: U covers X only when X = ⋃U and X ∉ U. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

An open γ-cover means an infinite open cover U such that each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
An open ω-cover means an open cover U such that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some member of U. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

S_fin(Γ,Ω) should be unpacked: for every sequence ⟨U_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ, there exist finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈ℕ} F_n is an ω-cover of X. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

U_fin(Γ,Ω) should be unpacked: it quantifies only over sequences ⟨U_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ in Γ such that no U_n contains a finite subcover, and asks for finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that {⋃F_n : n ∈ ℕ} is an ω-cover of X. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

Because X is a set of reals, the paper notes that the covers in Γ and Ω may be taken to be countable; adding this makes the question fully paper-faithful and stand-alone. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
refined_question: Let X ⊆ ℝ be a set of reals. Let Γ be the family of countable nontrivial open γ-covers of X and Ω the family of countable nontrivial open ω-covers of X, where a γ-cover is an infinite open cover U of X such that every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U, and an ω-cover is an open cover U of X such that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ U. Is the property U_fin(Γ,Ω)—for every sequence ⟨U_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ with no U_n containing a finite subcover, there exist finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that {⋃F_n : n ∈ ℕ} ∈ Ω—equivalent to S_fin(Γ,Ω)—for every sequence ⟨U_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ, there exist finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈ℕ} F_n ∈ Ω? If these two properties are not equivalent, does the Hurewicz property U_fin(Γ,Γ) nevertheless imply S_fin(Γ,Ω) for sets of reals? ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is not a broader neighboring conjecture but exactly Section 4, Problem 1, which asks these same two questions after the paper sets up the selection operators in Section 2.1, declares that the default scope is sets of reals in Section 2.3, defines open ω- and γ-covers in Section 3, and notes in Section 4 that the only unsettled implications in the classical diagram are the dotted ones. Your draft therefore targets Problem 1 directly; it mainly needs the formal definitions and cover conventions to become fully self-contained. ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))
